newsitem.title: MEXICO: Salinas y Rocha securitizes debt.
newsitem.headline: Salinas y Rocha securitizes debt.

text.p: Troubled Mexican retail chain Grupo Salinas y Rocha (GSYR) will securitize 2.148 billion pesos of debt held by four creditor banks, who will then hold 80 percent of the company's shareholding equity, the company chairman said on Thursday.

"The 2.148 billion pesos will be changed from debt to equity. Current shareholdings will be diluted to stand at 20 percent of equity, with creditors taking the remaiining 80 percent," GSYR Chairman Fernando Elizondo said at a news conference.
Elizondo said that of the 80 percent of equity to be held by creditor banks, and of that 49 percent will be redeemable preferred stock, with 31 percent common stock.
Current shareholders would retain control of the company, he added.
The creditor banks are Serfin, Banco Santander Mexicano, Confia and Bancomer, Elizondo said.
